Triage: lands in `packages/cli/test` e2e spawners (the "SHIPPED entrypoint" claim vs what `bin/run.js` actually resolves to under test); `pm:queue`, `domain:cli`, Task — test-truthfulness restoration, no product fork.

## Claim — `domain:cli` seat

Session `session_019siH5jDmk5hrayvfyojUqR`, branch `claude/issue-11317-e2e-shipped-entrypoint`. `pm:queue` → `pm:dispatched` and assignee set in one stroke, read back.

**Declared file surface**: `packages/cli/test/serve-mcp-stdio-answers.e2e.test.ts`, `packages/cli/test/serve-mcp-capability-collision.e2e.test.ts`, `packages/cli/test/serve-stdio-stdout-purity.e2e.test.ts`, and `packages/cli/vitest.config.ts` only where its cost header names these three files.

**Direction, from triage (`5386559160`)**: *"test-truthfulness restoration, no product fork."* That settles the card's open shape — the three files stop claiming an entrypoint they do not reach (the card's option 1: spawn `bin/run-dev.js` like the ~20 sibling e2e files, delete the false comment). Option 2 — genuinely reaching `dist/`, which needs a build dependency declared **and** another route to the `--dev` admin seed — is new engineering, not truthfulness restoration.

If the dev measures option 2 as cheap and fully inside the declared surface, ⛔ do not just take it: report the measurement and wait. Whichever lands, the comment and the code must agree afterwards — that agreement is the deliverable.

Adjacent, not a blocker: new finding #11441 reports that #11341's bare-`...process.env` worklist is two files short and one of them spawns a real `os serve`. Both #11341 and #11441 are ungraded `finding`s (not in flight, no conflict today), but they touch this neighbourhood — if the dev's own reading of these three spawners bears on that worklist, record it there rather than widening here.

**PR #11462 merged** (squash, `4e786cd8`) — reviewed and landed by the skills seat on the maintainer's live instruction (2026-08-24, verbatim: 「这几张你都帮我审核并合并吧」), after verifying the diff matches the triage-settled remedy (truthful entrypoint via `tsx bin/run-dev.js`, mechanism recorded in the corrected comments, `NODE_ENV` rationale) and 37/37 CI check-runs green at `4b7a8453`.

**This card stays OPEN — the deliberately-unclosed half is the PR's own "A ruling is needed" section**: option 2 (spawn `bin/run.js` with `NODE_ENV` unset so these three suites reach `packages/cli/dist`, the SHIPPED artifact) was rejected at triage on two facts that have both since become false — the build dependency is now declared (`#11268`) and the `--dev` seed no longer needs the parent's `NODE_ENV` (`serve.ts:1272`). Measured: option 2 passes all 3 files / 5 tests, is the fastest of the three shapes (30.3s vs this PR's 68.0s), and makes the original "shipped entrypoint" claim true. The standing counter-argument is repo policy: it couples three suites' verdicts to build state (a local `vitest` run against a stale `dist/` fails confusingly or worse), which the `check-test-source-alias` discipline exists to refuse — so it wants a guard (loud refusal on missing/stale dist + a lint pin on the `NODE_ENV` line) landed with it, not alone.

Maintainer's call, when convenient: **A** — take option 2 with the guard (shipped-artifact coverage 1 file → 4, these suites halve in time), or **B** — keep today's landed shape and close this card (shipped coverage stays with `serve-node-env-production-default.e2e.test.ts` alone). Either answer closes this card; nothing else in it is open.

## Closing — the fix landed. PR #11462 merged 2026-08-24T13:29:48Z.

`domain:cli` seat (#6024), session `019siH5jDmk5hrayvfyojUqR`.

**What landed:** the three files stop claiming an entrypoint they do not reach. They now spawn `bin/run-dev.js` through `tsx` like the sibling e2e files in the directory, and the false comment is replaced by the mechanism that made it false. 3 files / 5 tests, green on both sides of the change.

**Why this card closes rather than returning to the queue.** #11462 used `Part of`, not the closing keyword, and this seat's standing rule is that a `Part-of` merge returns the card to `pm:queue` with the assignee released. ⛔ Not applied here, deliberately: **the defect this card names is fixed, and there is no dev work left to dispatch.** A card sitting in `pm:queue` with nothing to implement is a card that will be claimed and handed back — the failure mode #8343 hit and had to be corrected out of with a ⛔ DO-NOT-DISPATCH comment. The mechanical rule exists for genuinely partial work; this is complete work whose author left the closing keyword off pending a ruling, which is a different situation and gets the treatment the PR body itself asked for: *"close the card by hand once the ruling lands."*

**The ruling:** the maintainer merged #11462 as-is at 13:29:48Z. As-is is option 1 — option 2 was one `NODE_ENV: 'development'` → `NODE_ENV: undefined` per file away and was not taken. Direction confirmed by the merge.

## The premise correction #11462 found, recorded here because this card carries the stale fact

This card's **fact (1) is false as of `main` today** and should not be quoted from again. It states `turbo.json` declares `"@objectstack/cli#test": { "dependsOn": ["^build"] }` — dependencies only, so `dist` is never built for these tests. It now reads `"dependsOn": ["build"]`, changed by #11268 (`918988ad`) — the same PR this card was filed from, whose change postdates this card's base (`adb1b9ea8c`).

Re-measured with this card's own instrument (`turbo run test --filter=@objectstack/cli --dry=json`): 58 tasks → 59, and `@objectstack/cli#test`'s resolved deps now **do** contain `@objectstack/cli#build`.

⇒ The defect survived on **fact (2) alone** — oclif's ts-path reroute — which is sufficient by itself. The conclusion stood; its cause is single, not composite.

⚠️ Also worth carrying: this card's body quotes `isProd()` **without its leading logical-NOT**, because a bang immediately before a bracket is image syntax and GitHub's sanitizer eats it — inside a code span and inside a fence alike. As quoted here the predicate is inverted, i.e. it reads as though oclif treats `development` and `test` as *production*. The source comments #11462 added carry the correct sign, because files are not sanitized. (Same class as the `<tag>` strip repaired on #8343 today; a body is not a safe place to quote a negation.)

## Residual, filed separately — ⛔ not left in this card's body to rot

Option 2 measured **faster than what landed** (17.68s vs 39.56s test time — the fastest of the three shapes) and is the only one that makes the original comment true, but it would make these three suites verdicts about **build state**, which `scripts/check-test-source-alias.mjs` and the `vitest.config.ts` header exist to refuse. That is a live trade-off, not a leftover task, and it outlives this card. Filed as a finding for triage to grade, together with the lint-rule question this card floated (making "spawns `bin/run.js`" and "sets a ts-path-enabling `NODE_ENV`" mutually exclusive, since the combination is silently self-cancelling).

Closing `completed`. Re-opening is free if the residual turns out to belong here after all.
